title: The cheapest gym floor option: stall mats
summary: Review of horse stall mats as home gym flooring. They are cheap, thick, absorb shock without bouncing, and can be moved and reused, unlike flimsy puzzle mats sold online. Downsides: slippery under the feet for squats, presses and bench leg drive, they feel like they steal drive energy, gather humidity, shift and crease, and don't fully protect against repeated deadlift drops, so he recommends two layers or plywood underneath.

claims.claim: Any pull where you put the bar down on the floor damages concrete over time, and it takes much less weight than you'd think to cause permanent damage.
Floor protection options are wood, rubber mats, or a combination of both as a platform.
Avoid the interlocking puzzle mats sold online: they are usually expensive, not thick enough, fall apart and keep coming unstuck.
Horse stall mats are the best home gym mats: the least expensive and the best at absorbing shock because they are thick and good quality.
Stall mats are easy to carry rolled up and taped, but when picking them up flat from a store warehouse, call ahead and bring a second person to stabilize them to avoid injury.
Good-quality stall mats don't bounce a dropped deadlift back at you; they absorb the shock, which is what they should do.
Stall mats feel too slippery for squats and overhead press, risky when walking out heavy squats, and your foot can slip during bench leg drive; wood feels like night and day.
He suspects, without proof, that soft mats absorb some of the energy you use to drive out of a squat, unlike solid wood; he can't squat on them.
In humid climates stall mats collect a thin layer of water, especially in the morning, making them even more slippery.
Even heavy mats shift and form creases that trap dust; he screwed his mats onto wooden planks for stability.
After about seven months of deadlifting on one spot over one layer of mat on wood, the wood underneath is sinking, so mats don't fully protect against shock.
If the floor underneath is sensitive, use two layers of stall mat or screw the mats onto cheap thin wood.

Stall mats are a good placeholder if you're unsure about building a platform, since they can later be reused in one; it's better to start small with home gym equipment than invest a lot at once without expertise.
